chapter.p: THE PROPHECY OF NEPHI, THE SON OF HELAMAN

p.i: God threatens the people of Nephi that he will visit them in his anger, to their utter destruction, except they repent of their wickedness. God smiteth the people of Nephi with pestilence; they repent and turn unto him. Samuel, a Lamanite, prophesies unto the Nephites.

chapter.li: LEChapter7 Verse1 Behold, now it came to pass in the sixty and ninth year of the reign of the judges over the people of the Nephites, that Nephi, the son of Helaman, returned to the land of Zarahemla from the land northward. VerseEnd Verse2 For he had been forth among the people who were in the land northward, and did preach the word of God unto them, and did prophesy many things unto them; VerseEnd Verse3 and they did reject all his words, insomuch that he could not stay among them, but returned again unto the land of his nativity. VerseEnd Verse4 And seeing the people in a state of such awful wickedness, and those Gaddianton robbers filling the judgment seats, having usurped the power and authority of the land, laying aside the commandments of God and not in the least aright before him, doing no justice unto the children of men, VerseEnd Verse5 condemning the righteous because of their righteousness, letting the guilty and the wicked go unpunished because of their money; and moreover, to be held in office at the head of government, to rule and do according to their wills, that they might get gain and glory of the world; and moreover, that they might the more easy commit adultery, and steal, and kill, and do according to their own wills — VerseEnd Verse6 now this great iniquity had come upon the Nephites in the space of not many years — and when Nephi saw it, his heart was swollen with sorrow within his breast. And he did exclaim in the agony of his soul, VerseEnd Verse7 Oh that I could have had my days in the days when my father Nephi first came out of the land of Jerusalem, that I could have joyed with him in the promised land! Then were his people easy to be entreated, firm to keep the commandments of God, and slow to be led to do iniquity, and they were quick to hearken unto the words of the Lord. VerseEnd Verse8 Yea, if my days could have been in those days, then would my soul have had joy in the righteousness of my brethren. VerseEnd Verse9 But behold, I am consigned that these are my days and that my soul shall be filled with sorrow because of this the wickedness of my brethren. VerseEnd

Verse10 And behold, now it came to pass that it was upon a tower which was in the garden of Nephi, which was by the highway which led to the chief market, which was in the city of Zarahemla. Therefore, as Nephi had bowed himself upon the tower which was in his garden — which tower was also near unto the garden gate which led by the highway — VerseEnd Verse11 and it came to pass that there were certain men passing by, and saw Nephi as he was a pouring out his soul unto God upon the tower; and they ran and told the people what they had seen. And the people came together in multitudes that they might know the cause of so great mourning for the wickedness of the people. VerseEnd

Verse12 And now when Nephi arose, he beheld the multitudes of people who had gathered together. VerseEnd Verse13 And it came to pass that he opened his mouth and said unto them, Behold, why have 2PP ye gathered yourselves together? That I may tell 2PP you of 2PP your iniquities? VerseEnd Verse14 Yea, because I have got upon my tower that I might pour out my soul unto my God because of the exceeding sorrow of my heart, which is because of 2PP your iniquities? VerseEnd Verse15 And because of my mourning and lamentation, 2PP ye have gathered yourselves together and do marvel, yea, and 2PP ye have great need to marvel; yea, 2PP ye had ought to marvel because 2PP ye are given away that the Devil has got so great hold upon 2PP your hearts. VerseEnd Verse16 Yea, how could 2PP ye have given away to the enticing of him who is seeking to hurl away 2PP your souls down to everlasting misery and endless woe? VerseEnd

Verse17 O repent 2PP ye, repent 2PP ye. Why will 2PP ye die? Turn 2PP ye, turn 2PP ye unto the Lord 2PP your God. Why has he forsaken 2PP you? VerseEnd Verse18 It is because 2PP you have hardened 2PP your hearts, yea, 2PP ye will not hearken unto the voice of the good shepherd; yea, 2PP ye have provoked him to anger against 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse19 And behold, instead of gathering 2PP you, except 2PP ye will repent, behold, he shall scatter 2PP you forth that 2PP ye shall become meat for dogs and wild beasts. VerseEnd Verse20 Oh how could 2PP you have forgotten 2PP your God in the very day that he has delivered 2PP you? VerseEnd Verse21 But behold, it is to get gain, to be praised of men, yea, and that 2PP ye might get gold and silver. And 2PP ye have set 2PP your hearts upon the riches and the vain things of this world, for the which 2PP ye do murder, and plunder, and steal, and bear false witness against 2PP your neighbor, and do all manner of iniquity; VerseEnd Verse22 and for this cause, woe shall come unto 2PP you except 2PP ye shall repent. For if 2PP ye will not repent, behold, this great city, and also all those great cities which are round about, which are in the land of our possession, shall be taken away, that 2PP ye shall have no place in them. For behold, the Lord will not grant unto 2PP you strength, as he has hitherto done, to withstand against 2PP your enemies. VerseEnd Verse23 For behold, thus saith the Lord: I will not shew unto the wicked of my strength, to one more than the other, save it be unto those who repent of their sins and hearken unto my words.

Now therefore I would that 2PP ye should behold, my brethren, that it shall be better for the Lamanites than for 2PP you, except 2PP ye shall repent. VerseEnd Verse24 For behold, they are more righteous than 2PP you, for they have not sinned against that great knowledge which 2PP ye have received; therefore, the Lord will be merciful unto them. Yea, he will lengthen out their days and increase their seed, even when 2PP thou shalt be utterly destroyed, except 2PP thou shalt repent. VerseEnd Verse25 Yea, woe be unto 2PP you because of that great abomination which has come among 2PP you, and 2PP ye have united yourselves unto it, yea, to that secret band which was established by Gaddianton. VerseEnd Verse26 Yea, woe shall come unto 2PP you because of that pride which 2PP ye have suffered to enter 2PP your hearts, which has lifted 2PP you up beyond that which is good because of 2PP your exceeding great riches. VerseEnd Verse27 Yea, woe be unto 2PP you because of 2PP your wickedness and abominations, VerseEnd Verse28 and except 2PP ye repent, 2PP ye shall perish. Yea, even 2PP your lands shall be taken from 2PP you and 2PP ye shall be destroyed from off the face of the earth. VerseEnd Verse29 Behold, now I do not say that these things shall be, of myself, because it is not of myself that I know these things. But behold, I know that these things are true because the Lord God has made them known unto me; therefore, I testify that they shall be. VerseEnd

LEChapter8 Verse1 And now it came to pass that when Nephi had said these words, behold, there were men who were judges who also belonged to the secret band of Gaddianton, and they were angry, and they cried out against him, saying unto the people, Why do 2PP ye not seize upon this man and bring him forth, that he may be condemned according to the crime which he has done? VerseEnd Verse2 Why seest 2PP thou this man and hearest him revile against this people and against our law? VerseEnd Verse3 For behold, Nephi had spoken unto them concerning the corruptness of their law. Yea, many things did Nephi speak which cannot be written; and nothing did he speak which were contrary to the commandments of God. VerseEnd Verse4 And those judges were angry with him because he spake plain unto them concerning their secret works of darkness; nevertheless, they durst not lay their own hands upon him, for they feared the people, lest they should cry out against them. VerseEnd Verse5 Therefore, they did cry unto the people, saying, Why do 2PP ye suffer this man to revile against us? For behold, he doth condemn all this people, even unto destruction, yea, and also that these our great cities shall be taken from us, that we shall have no place in them. VerseEnd Verse6 And now we know that this is impossible, for behold, we are powerful and our cities great, therefore our enemies can have no power over us. VerseEnd

Verse7 And it came to pass that thus they did stir up the people to anger against Nephi and raised contentions among them; for there were some who did cry out, Let this man alone, for he is a good man, and those things which he saith will surely come to pass except we repent. VerseEnd Verse8 Yea, behold, all the judgments will come upon us which he has testified unto us, for we know that he has testified aright unto us concerning our iniquities; and behold, they are many. And he knoweth as well all things which shall befall us as he knoweth our iniquities; VerseEnd Verse9 yea, and behold, if he had not been a prophet, he could not have testified concerning those things. VerseEnd

Verse10 And it came to pass that those people who sought to destroy Nephi were compelled, because of their fear, that they did not lay their hands on him. Therefore, he began again to speak unto them, seeing that he had gained favor in the eyes of some, insomuch that the remainder of them did fear. VerseEnd Verse11 Therefore, he was constrained to speak more unto them, saying, Behold, my brethren, have 2PP ye not read that God gave power unto one man, even Moses, to smite upon the waters of the Red Sea, and they departed hither and thither, insomuch that the Israelites, who were our fathers, came through upon dry ground, and the waters closed upon the armies of the Egyptians and swallowed them up? VerseEnd

Verse12 And now behold, if God gave unto this man such power, then why should 2PP ye dispute among yourselves and say that he hath given unto me no power whereby I may know concerning the judgments that shall come upon 2PP you except 2PP ye repent? VerseEnd Verse13 But behold, 2PP ye not only deny my words, but 2PP ye also deny all the words which hath been spoken by our fathers, and also the words which were spoken by this man, Moses, who had such great power given unto him — yea, the words which he hath spoken concerning the coming of the Messiah. VerseEnd Verse14 Yea, did he not bear record that the Son of God should come? And as he lifted up the brazen serpent in the wilderness, even so should he be lifted up who should come. VerseEnd Verse15 And as many as should look upon that serpent should live, even so as many as should look upon the Son of God with faith, having a contrite spirit, might live, even unto that life which is eternal. VerseEnd Verse16 And now behold, Moses did not only testify of these things, but also all the holy prophets from his day, even to the days of Abraham. VerseEnd Verse17 Yea, and behold, Abraham saw of his coming, and was filled with gladness and did rejoice. VerseEnd Verse18 Yea, and behold, I say unto 2PP you that Abraham not only knew of these things, but there were many before the days of Abraham who were called by the Order of God, yea, even after the Order of his Son — and this that it should be shewn unto the people a great many thousand years before his coming that even redemption should come unto them. VerseEnd Verse19 And now I would that 2PP ye should know that even since the days of Abraham there have been many prophets that have testified these things; yea, behold, the prophet Zenos did testify boldly, for the which he was slain, VerseEnd Verse20 and behold, also Zenoch, and also Ezaias, and also Isaiah, and Jeremiah, Jeremiah being that same prophet who testified of the destruction of Jerusalem — and now, we know that Jerusalem was destroyed according to the words of Jeremiah — oh then why not the Son of God come according to his prophecy? VerseEnd Verse21 And now will 2PP ye dispute that Jerusalem was not destroyed? Will 2PP ye say that the sons of Zedekiah were not slain, all except it were Muloch? Yea, and do 2PP ye not behold that the seed of Zedekiah are with us and they were driven out of the land of Jerusalem? But behold, this is not all. VerseEnd Verse22 Our father Lehi was driven out of Jerusalem because he testified of these things. Nephi also testified of these things, and also almost all of our fathers, even down to this time; yea, they have testified of the coming of Christ, and have looked forward and have rejoiced in his day which is to come. VerseEnd Verse23 And behold, he is God, and he is with them, and he did manifest himself unto them, that they were redeemed by him; and they gave unto him glory because of that which is to come. VerseEnd

Verse24 And now, seeing 2PP ye know these things and cannot deny them, except 2PP ye shall lie, therefore in this 2PP ye have sinned, for 2PP ye have rejected all these things, notwithstanding so many evidences which 2PP ye have received. Yea, even 2PP ye have received all things, both things in heaven and all things which are in earth, as a witness that they are true. VerseEnd Verse25 But behold, 2PP ye have rejected the truth and rebelled against 2PP your holy God. And even at this time, instead of laying up for yourselves treasures in Heaven, where nothing doth corrupt and where nothing can come which is unclean, 2PP ye are heaping up for yourselves wrath against the day of judgment. VerseEnd Verse26 Yea, even at this time 2PP ye are ripening because of 2PP your murders, and 2PP your fornication, and wickedness, for everlasting destruction. Yea, and except 2PP ye repent, it will come unto 2PP you soon; VerseEnd Verse27 yea, behold, it is now even at 2PP your doors. Yea, go 2PP ye in unto the judgment seat and search; and behold, 2PP your judge is murdered, and he lieth in his blood, and he hath been murdered by his brother who seeketh to sit in the judgment seat. VerseEnd Verse28 And behold, they both belong to 2PP your secret band whose author is Gaddianton and the Evil One who seeketh to destroy the souls of men. VerseEnd

LEChapter9 Verse1 Behold, now it came to pass that when Nephi had spoken these words, certain men who were among them ran to the judgment seat, yea, even there were five who went. And they said among themselves as they went, VerseEnd Verse2 Behold, now we will know of a surety whether this man be a prophet, and God hath commanded him to prophesy such marvelous things unto us. Behold, we do not believe that he hath, yea, we do not believe that he is a prophet; nevertheless, if this thing which he has said concerning the chief judge be true, that he be dead, then will we believe that the other words which he has spoken are true. VerseEnd Verse3 And it came to pass that they ran in their might and came in unto the judgment seat; and behold, the chief judge had fallen to the earth and did lie in his blood. VerseEnd Verse4 And now behold, when they saw this, they were astonished exceedingly, insomuch that they fell to the earth, for they had not believed the words which Nephi had spoken concerning the chief judge. VerseEnd Verse5 But now when they saw, they believed, and fear came upon them lest all the judgments which Nephi had spoken should come upon the people. Therefore, they did quake and had fallen to the earth. VerseEnd

Verse6 Now immediately when the judge had been murdered, he being stabbed by his brother, by a garb of secrecy, and he fled, and the servants ran and told the people, raising the cry of murder among them. VerseEnd Verse7 And behold, the people did gather themselves together unto the place of the judgment seat, and behold, to their astonishment they saw those five men who had fallen to the earth. VerseEnd Verse8 And now behold, the people knew nothing concerning the multitude which had gathered together at the garden of Nephi, therefore they said among themselves, These men are they who have murdered the judge, and God has smitten them that they could not flee from us. VerseEnd

Verse9 And it came to pass that they laid hold on them, and bound them, and cast them into prison. And there was a proclamation sent abroad that the judge was slain, and that the murderers had been taken and was cast into prison. VerseEnd Verse10 And it came to pass that on the morrow the people did assemble themselves together to mourn and to fast at the burial of the great and chief judge who had been slain. VerseEnd Verse11 And thus were also those judges, who were at the garden of Nephi and heard his words, were also gathered together at the burial. VerseEnd

Verse12 And it came to pass that they inquired among the people, saying, Where are the five who were sent to inquire concerning the chief judge, whether he was dead? And they answered and said, Concerning the five whom 2PP ye say 2PP ye have sent, we know not, but there are five who are the murderers whom we have cast into prison. VerseEnd Verse13 And it came to pass that the judges desired that they should be brought, and they were brought; and behold, they were the five who were sent. And behold, the judges inquired of them to know concerning the matter. And they told them all that they had done, saying, VerseEnd Verse14 We ran and came to the place of the judgment seat; and when we saw all things even as Nephi had testified, we were astonished, insomuch that we fell to the earth. And when we were recovered from our astonishment, behold, they cast us into prison. VerseEnd Verse15 Now as for the murder of this man, we know not who has done it; and only this much we know, we ran and came according as 2PP ye desired, and behold, he was dead according to the words of Nephi. VerseEnd

Verse16 And now it came to pass that the judges did expound the matter unto the people, and did cry out against Nephi, saying, Behold, we know that this Nephi must have agreed with someone to slay the judge, and then he might declare it unto us, that he might convert us unto his faith, that he might raise himself to be a great man, chosen of God and a prophet. VerseEnd Verse17 And now behold, we will detect this man, and he shall confess his fault and make known unto us the true murderer of this judge. VerseEnd Verse18 And it came to pass that the five were liberated on the day of the burial. Nevertheless, they did rebuke the judges in the words which they had spoken against Nephi, and did contend with them one by one, insomuch that they did confound them. VerseEnd

Verse19 Nevertheless, they caused that Nephi should be taken, and bound, and brought before the multitude; and they began to question him in divers ways, that they might cross him, that they might accuse him to death, VerseEnd Verse20 saying unto him, 2PSI Thou art confederate. Who is this man that hath done this murder? Now tell us and acknowledge 2PSI thy fault; saying, Behold, here is money; and also, we will grant unto 2PSI thee 2PSI thy life if 2PSI thou wilt tell us and acknowledge the agreement which 2PSI thou hast made with him. VerseEnd Verse21 But Nephi said unto them, O 2PP ye fools, 2PP ye uncircumcised of heart, 2PP ye blind and 2PP ye stiffnecked people, do 2PP ye know how long the Lord 2PP your God will suffer 2PP you that 2PP ye shall go on in this 2PP your ways of sin? VerseEnd Verse22 O 2PP ye had ought to begin to howl and mourn because of the great destruction at this time which doth await 2PP you except 2PP ye shall repent. VerseEnd Verse23 Behold, 2PP ye say that I have agreed with a man that he should murder Seezoram, our chief judge. But behold, I say unto 2PP you that this is because I have testified unto 2PP you, that 2PP ye might know concerning this thing, yea, even for a witness unto 2PP you that I did know of the wickedness and abominations which are among 2PP you. VerseEnd Verse24 And because I have done this, 2PP ye say that I have agreed with a man that he should do this thing. Yea, because I shewed unto 2PP you this sign, 2PP ye are angry with me and seek to destroy my life. VerseEnd

Verse25 And now behold, I will shew unto 2PP you another sign, and see if 2PP ye will in this thing seek to destroy me. VerseEnd Verse26 Behold, I say unto 2PP you, go to the house of Seantum, who is the brother of Seezoram, and say unto him, VerseEnd Verse27 Has Nephi, the pretended prophet who doth prophesy so much evil concerning this people, agreed with 2PSI thee, in the which 2PSF ye have murdered Seezoram, who is 2PSF your brother? VerseEnd Verse28 And behold, he shall say unto 2PP you, Nay. VerseEnd Verse29 And 2PP ye shall say unto him, Have 2PSF ye murdered 2PSF your brother? VerseEnd Verse30 And he shall stand with fear and wist not what to say. And behold, he shall deny unto 2PP you, and he shall make as if he were astonished; nevertheless, he shall declare unto 2PP you that he is innocent. VerseEnd Verse31 But behold, 2PP ye shall examine him, and 2PP ye shall find blood upon the skirts of his cloak. VerseEnd Verse32 And when 2PP ye have seen this, 2PP ye shall say, From whence cometh this blood? Do we not know that it is the blood of 2PP your brother? VerseEnd Verse33 And then shall he tremble and shall look pale, even as if death had come upon him. VerseEnd Verse34 And then shall 2PP ye say, Because of this fear and this paleness which has come upon 2PSF your face, behold, we know that 2PSI thou art guilty. VerseEnd Verse35 And then shall greater fear come upon him; and then shall he confess unto 2PP you, and deny no more that he has done this murder. VerseEnd Verse36 And then shall he say unto 2PP you that I, Nephi, knew nothing concerning the matter, save it were given unto me by the power of God. And then shall 2PP ye know that I am an honest man and that I am sent unto 2PP you from God. VerseEnd

Verse37 And it came to pass that they went and did even according as Nephi had said unto them. And behold, the words which he had said were true; for according to the words, he did deny, and also according to the words, he did confess. VerseEnd Verse38 And he was brought to prove that he himself was the very murderer, insomuch that the five were set at liberty, and also was Nephi. VerseEnd Verse39 And there were some of the Nephites who believed on the words of Nephi; and there were some also who believed because of the testimony of the five, for they had been converted while they were in prison. VerseEnd Verse40 And now there were some among the people who said that Nephi was a prophet; VerseEnd Verse41 and there were others who said, Behold, he is a god, for except he was a god, he could not know of all things. For behold, he has told us the thoughts of our hearts, and also has told us things, and even he has brought unto our knowledge the true murderer of our chief judge. VerseEnd

LEChapter10 Verse1 And it came to pass that there arose a division among the people, insomuch that they divided hither and thither and went their ways, leaving Nephi alone as he was standing in the midst of them. VerseEnd Verse2 And it came to pass that Nephi went his way towards his own house, pondering upon the things which the Lord had shewn unto him. VerseEnd Verse3 And it came to pass as he was thus pondering, being much cast down because of the wickedness of the people of the Nephites, their secret works of darkness, and their murderings, and their plunderings, and all manner of iniquities — and it came to pass as he was thus pondering in his heart, behold, a voice came unto him, saying, VerseEnd Verse4 Blessed art 2PSI thou, Nephi, for those things which 2PSI thou hast done. For I have beheld how 2PSI thou hast with unwearyingness declared the word which I have given unto 2PSI thee, unto this people. And 2PSI thou hast not feared them, and hast not sought 2PSI thine own life, but hath sought my will and to keep my commandments. VerseEnd Verse5 And now because 2PSI thou hast done this with such unwearyingness, behold, I will bless 2PSI thee for ever. And I will make 2PSI thee mighty in word and in deed, in faith and in works, yea, even that all things shall be done unto 2PSI thee according to 2PSI thy word, for 2PSI thou shalt not ask that which is contrary to my will. VerseEnd Verse6 Behold, 2PSI thou art Nephi, and I am God. Behold, I declare it unto 2PSI thee in the presence of mine angels that 2PSF ye shall have power over this people and shall smite the earth with famine, and with pestilence, and destruction, according to the wickedness of this people. VerseEnd Verse7 Behold, I give unto 2PSF you power that whatsoever 2PSF ye shall seal on earth shall be sealed in Heaven, and whatsoever 2PSF ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in Heaven. And thus shall 2PSF ye have power among this people. VerseEnd Verse8 And thus, if 2PSF ye shall say unto this temple, It shall be rent in twain — and it shall be done. VerseEnd Verse9 And if 2PSF ye shall say unto this mountain, Be 2PSI thou cast down and become smooth — and it shall be done. VerseEnd Verse10 And behold, if 2PSF ye shall say that God shall smite this people, it shall come to pass. VerseEnd Verse11 And now behold, I command 2PSF you that 2PSF ye shall go and declare unto this people that thus saith the Lord God, who is the Almighty: Except 2PP ye repent, 2PP ye shall be smitten, even unto destruction. VerseEnd

Verse12 And behold, now it came to pass that when the Lord had spoken these words unto Nephi, he did stop and did not go unto his own house, but did return unto the multitudes who were scattered about upon the face of the land, and began to declare unto them the word of the Lord which had been spoken unto him concerning their destruction if they did not repent. VerseEnd Verse13 Now behold, notwithstanding that great miracle which Nephi had done in telling them concerning the death of the chief judge, they did harden their hearts and did not hearken unto the words of the Lord; VerseEnd Verse14 therefore, Nephi did declare unto them the word of the Lord, saying, Except 2PP ye repent, thus saith the Lord, 2PP ye shall be smitten, even unto destruction. VerseEnd Verse15 And it came to pass that when Nephi had declared unto them the word, behold, they did still harden their hearts, and would not hearken unto his words. Therefore they did revile against him and did seek to lay their hands upon him, that they might cast him into prison. VerseEnd Verse16 But behold, the power of God was with him and they could not take him to cast him into prison, for he was taken by the spirit and conveyed away out of the midst of them. VerseEnd

Verse17 And it came to pass that thus he did go forth in the spirit from multitude to multitude, declaring the word of God, even until he had declared it unto them all, or sent it forth among all the people. VerseEnd Verse18 And it came to pass that they would not hearken unto his words. And there began to be contentions, insomuch that they were divided against themselves, and began to slay one another with the sword. VerseEnd Verse19 And thus ended the seventy and first year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi. VerseEnd
